paragraphs.text: 在windows平台用everything实现@file
# dsh-at-file-everything
Everything-index search for DeepSeek Harness on Windows, through `es.exe`: instant `@file` completio
n for a human, and a `find_files` tool for the model — both answered from the same Everything index.
> 中文说明见 README.zh.md。
## Why
Two callers need to find files, and neither is served well by walking the tree.
**The human typing `@`.** The shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-file-reference-local` provider answers from
a workspace walk it performs itself, bounded by `maxEntries`. In a large tree that walk is both slow
and lossy. On the Unity project this plugin was written for:
| | upstream walk | this plugin |
| what it searches | every file under the workspace root | Everything's index, scoped with `-path` |

| entry budget | `maxEntries` (50 000 by default) | none |
| first `@` of a session | full traversa

l | ~80 ms |
| warm query | re-ranks a bounded index | ~70–80 ms |
| coverage | ~469 k of ~1.5 M fil

es, after tuning | the whole scope |
| heap | ~99 MB for the index | none held by the provider |
A concrete failure the upstream budget caused: ~1.2 M files under `Library/` and ~270 k under `Outpu
t/` exhausted the index before any `Assets/` source was reached, so `@PlayablePrefab` answered `Libr
ary/*` noise while the real file was missing.
**The model resolving a path.** It has `glob` and the shell, and both walk the tree with the same bu
dget problem. `find_files` answers from the index instead — the same lookup that makes `@` fast, exp
osed where the agent can call it.
Everything already maintains that index machine-wide as a Windows service, so both surfaces answer f
rom it and walk nothing.
## Requirements
- **Windows.** The plugin declares `os: win32`; on other platforms Everything does not exist and the

plugin has nothing to answer from.
- **Everything running and indexing.** The plugin queries it; it
does not bundle or start it.
Check the environment before blaming the plugin:

### Why the card must also be claimed on the Host

A browser card alone is not enough. The Plugins page asks the Host whether the
namespace still wants
its page auto-generated:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The default is `true`, so a plugin that only registers a slot in
`plugins.bundle.config` gets a **ge

neric form built from its Config schema**, and
its own card is never drawn. With a volatile-only sch

ema that generic form has
nothing useful to render, which is how a blank-looking page happens.

So the Host half claims the page explicitly, exactly as every first-party plugin
with a custom page

e Host half claims the page explicitly, exactly as every first-party plugin
with a custom page does:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Three consequences worth remembering:

- **Claim it only if the card actually exists.** With `auto: false` and no
registered card the page

is empty — worse than the generic form. That is why the
browser half now registers on both slots unc

onditionally, wraps each in
`try`/`catch`, and does not bail out when `configForms` is unreachable;

the card
renders its own "not available" notice instead.
- **The slot key is the package name**, whi

le the *settings namespace* is the
Loader entry id (`file-reference-everything` here). Both strings

are needed:
`plugins.bundle.config` matches the page's inventory by package name, and
`configForms.g

et()` takes the entry id.
- **`ctx.locale.bind(ns)` returns a lookup function, not a copy table.** I

t answers
`t('some.key')`; reading its result as `{ label, hint }` yields `undefined` for
every capt

ion while data-driven inputs still render — a card of empty boxes that
reads like a layout bug. This

plugin therefore keeps its copy as a literal table
in `src/client.ts` and asks the locale service o

nly *which language* to use.
`test/render.test.js` expands the component the way React does and fail

s when any
caption goes missing, which is the check that would have caught it.
### Why the lists are empty by default

What should be hidden is a property of the project, not of the plugin. A Unity
tree wants `Library`

and `Output`, a Rust one `target`, a monorepo neither — and a
shipped default silently hides real so

urces on the first two while doing nothing
useful on the third. The card is where this is decided.
### Why two query-level lists instead of one

Everything parses the two differently. A folder is named by its exact path
segment (`!\Library\`), w

hile a file is named by a pattern (`!*.meta`). There are
also two other spellings that look right an

e is named by a pattern (`!*.meta`). There are
also two other spellings that look right and are not:
| Term | What it actually does |
| `!path:Library` | Matches the *string* anywhere in the path, so it also drops `Library.txt` and `L

ibraryBeta`. |
| `!folder:Library` | Matches the folder row but **not** its contents, so the subtree

!folder:Library` | Matches the folder row but **not** its contents, so the subtree stays. |
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations
- **Windows only**, and only as good as the Everything index. Files excluded from indexing are invis

ible here too — to `find_files` as well as to `@`.
- **Everything must be running.** If the service
is down the plugin logs that specific cause, completion answers nothing, and `find_files` raises an
error naming the cause and pointing at `glob`. The bundled `es.exe` supplies the *client*, not the s

ervice, so it cannot help here.
- **The bundled client is pinned.** It is chosen for Everything 1.4
latency (see `bin/README.md`). On a future Everything whose `count:` filter is cheap, a newer client
would be the better pin; a user-supplied `es.exe` on `PATH` or in `esCommand` always takes preceden

ce, so this only affects machines relying on the fallback.
- **Filename-scoped search.** Typing a di
rectory path with `/` lists that directory, but a bare query will not match deep path fragments that
no file name contains — the upstream substring path match was traded for the ~30× latency of the in

dex path. `find_files` searches names only, so the same applies.
- **`find_files` pages, it does not
stream.** One call returns at most 500 entries; past that the model must narrow the query or page b

y raising `limit`. The result says so.
- **One `es.exe` process per query.** Each query is a fresh p

rocess (~70–80 ms warm). Cancellation kills it.
- **First query after Everything's index is cold** c
an take ~1 s as the service pages the index in; `timeoutMs` covers that wait, `deadlineMs` covers th
s as the service pages the index in; `timeoutMs` covers that wait, `deadlineMs` covers the process.
